newsitem.title: USA: Dade Cty, Fla, official seeks change in Miami vote.
newsitem.headline: Dade Cty, Fla, official seeks change in Miami vote.

text.p: A Dade County commissioner has proposed changing the county charter to give residents in unincorporated areas a vote in an upcoming referendum on whether to dissolve the city of Miami, aides said Thursday.
The commissioner, Pedro Reboredo, was unavailable for comment Thursday but planned a Friday afternoon news conference to outline his plan.
Miami is one of 29 municipalities in Dade County and is the county seat.
Earlier this month, Miami residents collected enough petition signatures to force a referendum on a proposal to dissolve the city.

The sponsors of the dissolution movement, led by attorney Gene Stearns, said Miami's struggle to close a $68 million deficit and the recent federal corruption charges against top leaders were proof that city officials were incapable of governing.
Stearns acknowledged that allowing unincorporated residents to vote would make it more difficult to dissolve the city.
"If you're a county taxpayer, why in the world would you want (Miami's) problems?" Stearns told the Fort Lauderdale Sun-Sentinel.

Under the current county charter, only city of Miami residents can vote on whether to dissolve the city. If it is dissolved, it would be absorbed into the Dade County government, which provides services to residents of unincorporated areas.
Reboredo said it was only fair that suburban residents have a voice because their tax rates and quality of services could be affected if the county absorbs Miami.

Under election rules, Miami has until August to vote on the dissolution. A vote to change the charter could be held no sooner than April 7, and would have to be approved by at least nine of the 13 county commissioners.
